transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-03-12
Start Time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 37 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM) — Alicia Park (HelioHealth ML Lead), Tom Brenner (SRE), Sanjay Patel (Security), Lena Ortiz (Product)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding progress, access setup, and environment readiness for HelioHealth pilot. Main blockers: VPC peering details, service account roles, KMS key policy clarity, and a minor firewall rule. SE provided preliminary tuning recommendations and agreed to run a small latency baseline. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics Covered:
- Access provisioning status (service accounts, roles, SSO)
- Network connectivity: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, firewall rules
- Security controls: KMS, audit logging, retention
- Early perf/latency check and config tuning (batching, kv-cache)
- Timeline for pilot milestones

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh we'll do a quick 30ish minute sync, go through the access checklist and then Diego will run through the tuning notes and then we can set action items. Sound good?
[00:17] Alicia: yes, that works for us, thanks Maya. quick context, we spun up the test VPC last night and tried the peering template but hit an odd route overlap with our analytics cluster. so that's where we're stuck.
[00:35] Tom: yeah the CIDR ranges overlapped so the peering got rejected, and our security team doesn't want us to reassign existing subnets.
[00:48] Maya: got it, okay thank you. Diego, maybe you can remind the group of the other connectivity option — PrivateLink — and tradeoffs?
[01:03] Diego: sure, so PrivateLink avoids cross-VPC routing by creating an endpoint service, so it's a bit simpler for orgs that can't change CIDRs. tradeoff is it requires endpoint creation in each AZ and costs slightly more for data egress; latency typically microseconds higher but not material for our 95th percentile goals. for the pilot, if HelioHealth prefers minimal infra changes, PrivateLink is a good fallback.
[01:34] Sanjay: are there any extra audit logs we lose with PrivateLink compared to peering?
[01:41] Diego: no, audit logs still flow — the control plane events are unchanged — but we will need to ensure flow logs are enabled on the endpoint; Redwood provides a helper script for that.
[01:55] Priya: Maya, did you already send the template for VPC peering?
[02:01] Maya: I posted the peering template in the shared drive; I'll also email a trimmed diagram that highlights the problematic CIDR fields so Tom can share with infra.
[02:11] Alicia: great, that will help. also quick question on service accounts: we created an svc-redwood user but we weren't sure which IAM roles are required for the pilot.
[02:24] Diego: minimal roles are: read/write to the bucket used for eval artifacts, an sts assume role for the runtime, and network egress permissions. we'll put an explicit least-priv policy in the notes; for KMS, the runtime needs decrypt/encrypt on the model key.
[02:42] Sanjay: on KMS, we have an existing key policy that restricts usage to certain service principals. is there a way for Redwood to be added without creating a new key?
[02:52] Diego: yes, you can add Redwood's service principal — we'll provide the principal id — or you can create a dedicated key for the pilot, whichever is simpler given your compliance rules. adding the principal is fine if security approves.
[03:05] Lena: any concerns about data residency? we're based in US but some patient meta could be EU-sourced.
[03:13] Maya: good call — for the pilot we recommended hosting the inference in east-us region but if datasets are EU, we should limit data movement. we can show a per-route routing policy and fallbacks to a EU host in Dedicated if needed.
[03:29] Tom: okay that's helpful. next, I ran the lightweight smoke test from the quickstart and saw tokenized errors in one of the containers — something about missing model weights.
[03:42] Diego: that usually indicates the model cache wasn't pre-seeded; our quickstart can auto-pull the model if you have outbound egress. did you see a 403 or a connection timeout?
[03:53] Tom: 403 on S3 get_object for the model shard.
[03:58] Diego: then it's an IAM issue for the svc account; check the bucket policy and the assume-role mapping. I'll send a sample bucket policy snip.
[04:10] Alicia: for the performance baseline, what's realistic for us to measure this week? we want 95th percentile latency under 350ms for 256 tokens.
[04:20] Diego: for the hosted path we can likely show that. for Private/on-prem it depends on GPU type and NVLink packing. for the pilot, let's run a synthetic with 100 concurrent streams at 1 RPS each, 256-token prompts, and report p50/p95/p99.
[04:40] Maya: agreed. Diego, can you supply the synthetic runner and the config?
[04:46] Diego: yes, I'll attach a JMX/postman script and a lightweight python harness that hits the inference endpoint; it includes batching flags you can toggle.
[04:56] Sanjay: are there any encryption-in-transit certs we need to import? our infra team uses custom CA for internal endpoints.
[05:05] Diego: Redwood supports mTLS for Dedicated and private installs; for hosted we'll do standard TLS with CA chain trust. if you're using a custom internal CA you might need to add the CA to the runtime trust store; Tom, is that the case?
[05:20] Tom: yes, it's our internal CA. we'll either add it or use a gateway that does TLS termination.
[05:26] Priya: a quick note on onboarding: we've seen the fastest pilots when the customer's SRE sets up the service account and grants roles so the SE can validate the runtime; if Helio can do that by Monday we could run the baseline Tuesday.
[05:40] Alicia: we can aim for Monday. Tom will provision.
[05:45] Maya: perfect. Diego, can you review tuning notes now?
[05:50] Diego: yup. so the pilot chosen model is gpt-xl-emu (note: placeholder name) — we've got two config knobs that matter most: batching window and kv-cache eviction. for shorter prompts, reduce max_batch_latency to 8ms to keep p95 low; for throughput experiments bump it to 40ms. suggestion: start at 12ms and measure.
[06:15] Diego: caching: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts; that reduced token compute by ~18% in a recent internal test. also consider quantized weights if memory pressure shows.
[06:28] Alicia: interesting, how disruptive is quantization to quality?
[06:32] Diego: typically minor for classification and embeddings; generative tasks vary. we do recommend running eval set comparisons — Redwood Optimize can automate that.
[06:42] Lena: can Redwood run the eval? we don't have a ready eval harness yet.
[06:46] Diego: yes, we can run an eval against your labeled set; there's a small fee for managed evals but for the pilot we'll include a one-off run. you'll need to upload the test prompts and reference outputs to the shared bucket.
[06:58] Alicia: ok we'll prepare that — maybe 500 prompts.
[07:02] Maya: good. quick question from my side: what's the expected cost footprint for this pilot week? ballpark is fine.
[07:11] Diego: for a small pilot running ~10k tokens/day on hosted, maybe $40–80 depending on model. Dedicated numbers would be higher up-front but lower per-token at scale. we'll send a cost estimate spreadsheet.
[07:26] Maya: will do. Sanjay, on compliance: any blockers for us adding Redwood to the KMS policy?
[07:33] Sanjay: we need a PR review and a short risk study. if Maya sends the principal and the exact permissions we'll run the review this week.
[07:44] Maya: I'll send principal today.
[07:46] 
[08:00] (brief side chatter about calendar invites and who owns the doc links)

[08:20] Diego: one more note about benchmarking — please try to run the baseline from a host inside the same AZ if possible, cross-AZ numbers will skew latency.
[08:31] Tom: noted, we'll run from the analytics-1 AZ.

[08:40] Priya: Action recap time?
[08:44] Maya: yep, quick recap — Tom to fix CIDR peering or opt for PrivateLink, Tom to provision service account and roles, Sanjay to validate KMS policy, Diego to send runner and config, Maya to send peering diagram and security docs. we'll meet same time next week and review latency numbers. anyone want to add?
[09:08] Alicia: nothing else from me. thanks.
[09:12] Maya: awesome, thanks all. we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.

End of transcript
